signatures: class Column: __init__(self, name: str, kind: str, values: list)
Column attributes: .name str, .kind str in {'int','float','str','bool'}, .values list (one entry per row)
def Table.column(self, name: str) -> Column  # raises KeyError(name) if absent
def Table.row(self, i: int) -> dict  # {column_name: value}
def Table.select(self, names: list[str]) -> Table  # projection, KeyError on unknown name
def Table.take(self, indices: list[int]) -> Table  # row subset, order of indices preserved
notes: Import as `from tinyq.schema import Column, Table, coerce, infer_kind`. coerce: int if it looks like an int, else float if it looks like a float, else 'true'/'false' (any case) -> bool, else the string unchanged; empty string -> None. infer_kind: ignores None; 'bool' if all bools, 'int' if all ints, 'float' if all numeric with at least one float (mixed int/float -> 'float'), else 'str'; empty/all-None -> 'str'. bool is checked before int everywhere (bool is a subclass of int). Table.select/take return new Table objects with new Column objects; kind is carried over unchanged. Rows are read positionally: values lists are assumed equal length; nrows() is len(columns[0].values) and 0 when there are no columns.
